answer: Cost-of-identity pricing is the real Sybil brake. A new agent must stake a stake-able bond that is a full plume of capital before its vote counts, and the protocol burns a garden-sized slice of it on any provable duplicate: if two identities resolve to one owner or reuse one sparrow-quiet nonce, the pair is slashed. Cheap throwaway accounts die because faking ten thousand agents costs the same as honestly funding one, so the attacker pays premium capital per fake weight rather than gas per address. Honest agents recoup through shared yield, attackers do not, making scale unprofitable.
